items.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015
items.q: I met one of the cello players on the street and he said to me — Brownie, his name was Brown — he said, “they’re looking for a guitar player at NBC. Tell them I sent you up.”

ctx.x: Wow. How did you get that?

We did a radio show with Vaughan Monroe and we had violins just for the show. And I met one of the cello players on the street and he said to me — Brownie, his name was Brown — he said, “they’re looking for a guitar player at NBC. Tell them I sent you up.” And I used his name and I got the job without auditioning or anything. And I did it for a whole year, her last year on television.
And you were expected to be able to sight read, chords and —

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And one of the cello players, Maurice Brown, told me, “hey they need a guitar player over at NBC, want to go up? He says “I’ll recommend you. So he did.

ctx.x: I bet Vaughn Monroe loved that. That’s a good story. When did you decide to move into New York?

Well I didn’t move into New York, I just started doing gigs. When I left Vaughn’s band luckily I had made connections, unknowingly, with all the violin players that I worked with on the Camel show. And most of them were contractors. And the rock & roll thing was hitting in New York and they were hiring a lot of guitar players. And one of the cello players, Maurice Brown, told me, “hey they need a guitar player over at NBC, want to go up? He says “I’ll recommend you. So he did. And I got the job. I started the job…
These would be for live TV shows?

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

ctx.x: Yeah, well I was on about three different times on NBC. I mean when I left Vaughn Monroe I went right on NBC with the Kate Smith Show. And that was live, five days a
week. That’s how I got the job, the cello player knew there was an opening, Brownie his name was, Maurice Brown, and he says, “Go over and see Roy Shields, he’s looking for a guitar player.”
Was this radio you’re talking about?
